notes.title: Redesign of the game graphics and assets.
notes.content:
Hello everyone, after a long period of work on [b]"Disasters Escape: The Island"[/b], I realized a significant performance issue stemming from the use of UE5. Specifically, I was utilizing [b]global illumination (Lumen)[/b], as you can see in the attached photos. While this global illumination added remarkable graphical details, it made the game visually stunning but caused a substantial drop in performance, with frame rates ranging between [b]20-40 fps[/b] on a [u]mid-range graphics card[/u].

I resolved this issue through a redesign of the graphics, and I'm here to show it to you. The graphics may appear somewhat less detailed, but I assure you that in a game, graphics represent only 10-20% of the overall experience. Below, you'll find some images showing how global illumination worked before and after. Additionally, I'm providing a small spoiler of what the optimized graphics will look like. Thank you for your patience, and I wish you a rewarding wait until 2024 (barring unforeseen circumstances).

[h2]Lumen[/h2]

[b]Image without global illumination (Lumen):[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44132731/67f4a00ec509c0d4204190972dbcd591b1474b17.png[/img]

[b]Image with global illumination (Lumen):[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44132731/d965e7a00e1863f4edacb1c54beaceedcca5e4ec.png[/img]



Wait, you might be wondering, couldn't you just disable it? Well, it wasn't that simple because all assets were specifically designed to work with Lumen. ːsteamfacepalmː

[h2]New Graphics!![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44132731/9328dd61f4f1b99cfb0feb75dc013705c91bb004.png[/img]

This is a gameplay image from a cinematic camera without Lumen.
